slides.headline: She was born in Kerala. On November 3, 2026, she was elected the first South Asian woman to lead Los Angeles.
Nithya Raman is the Mayor-elect of Los Angeles, after defeating incumbent Karen Bass
slides.body: Born in Kerala, India, in 1981, Raman moved to the US with her family around age six, eventually settling near Boston. She studied at Harvard, then earned a master's in urban planning from MIT in 2008. Bass conceded on November 5, 2026, calling the transition 'smooth and seamless.'

slides.headline: Before City Hall, she co-founded a homelessness nonprofit and led Time's Up Entertainment.
slides.body: Raman became an LA City Councilmember for District 4 in December 2020. Her mayoral win makes her the first South Asian woman to lead Los Angeles - and means both Los Angeles and New York are now led by Indian-origin mayors.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat benefits every time Indian-origin leadership reaches the top of a major global institution.
slides.body: Raman's path - from Kerala to Harvard and MIT to the mayor's office of America's second-largest city - is one more data point in how far an Indian upbringing can carry someone who takes public service seriously.
